title: The king cobra is now four species
storyboard: Film: naturalist to camera by a Western Ghats stream, waist-up, 2 takes; drop into the pip inset

scenes.headline: The king cobra just became four species
Ours is Ophiophagus kaalinga
scenes.body: The Western Ghats king cobra. 'Kaalinga' is the Kannada name for the king cobra. (Photo: Kannur, Kerala)

scenes.headline: Count the body bands
scenes.body: Western Ghats: fewer than 40. Northern: 40–70. Sunda: more than 70.
scenes.source: Das et al. 2024, European Journal of Taxonomy 961

scenes.headline: Smaller ranges, new risks
scenes.body: One 'Vulnerable' species is now four, each with a smaller range. Each may need its own protection; current antivenom may not cover all four.

caption:
One king, four kingdoms.

The 2024 revision rests on 153 specimens plus earlier genetic work: Northern (O. hannah), Sunda (O. bungarus), Western Ghats (O. kaalinga) and Luzon (O. salvatana) king cobras.

Source: Das et al. 2024, European Journal of Taxonomy; Mongabay-India.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Presenter-led commentary: pip inset is a placeholder for a naturalist explaining the Oct 2024 taxonomy paper; original because it localises the news to the Western Ghats species.
